extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers and creative writers interested in epistolary techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting stories told through letters, emails, diary entries, postcards, and similar written forms, focusing on voice, plot progression, authenticity, and information reveal. Includes examples and prompts to spark ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Each character's voice should be distinct in their writing style, tone, and vocabulary, reflecting their personality and emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure characters' written voices differ so readers can identify who is 'speaking' on the page; let vocabulary, tone, sentence length, and emotional color convey personality and inner life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Arc
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan a clear narrative arc that progresses through the letters, emails, or diary entries, ensuring the story unfolds naturally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though the story is delivered in fragments, map out a coherent beginning, middle, and end across entries so momentum and stakes increase and the reader feels a satisfying progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediacy and Authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the immediacy of the medium to lend authenticity to the narrative; characters can express their emotions in real-time, making readers feel intimately connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage the 'as-it-happens' quality of personal documents (diaries, emails, letters) to create intimacy. Favor believable, context-appropriate language and spontaneous details that feel true to the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revealing Information Gradually
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the format to reveal key information gradually, building tension and curiosity as readers piece together the puzzle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stagger revelations across entries so the reader actively assembles the story; avoid dumping backstory—let clues and conflicting accounts create intrigue and momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple Perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize multiple characters' perspectives to provide a well-rounded view of the story's events and conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Switching correspondents or document types can offer contrast, unreliable narrators, and fuller understanding; ensure each perspective adds distinct information or emotional resonance rather than repeating the same facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose Appropriate Epistolary Forms & Prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the specific epistolary forms (letters, emails, diary entries, postcards, etc.) and scenarios (time capsule, diary exchange, email correspondence, historical letters) that best serve the story's emotional and structural needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match form to tone and plot: emails suit contemporary voice and immediacy, postcards constrain detail and heighten implication, soldier letters evoke historical distance and emotion. Use prompts such as 'Time Capsule', 'Diary Exchange', 'Email Correspondence', 'Historical Letters', and 'Postcard Story' as starting frameworks.
